body:
Ultimately, all link `rel`s are for machine consumption: we don't mint them with an eye toward users right-clicking and choosing "Inspect element" or "View source". So maintaining the `rel` database hinges crucially on what user agents and other machines plan to do with them.

I suspect that, even if Google is planning to "offload" `nofollow` (unsure what that means?), there are still plenty of pieces of software that will want to use it. So I don't think we should remove it or deprecate it. We could certainly tighten up the definition; the way to do that would be to do more research into what existing software does with it.

Similarly, I don't think we should invent new rels (`unendorsed`, etc.) unless we have signals that software is planning to use them. (Including, e.g., your suggested user experiences of user agents showing a warning.)

As for `sponsored` and `ugc`, I am unsure whether they should be put in the main spec or in the [extension to the predefined set of link types](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#other-link-types) wiki registry. The division seems somewhat historical, e.g. I'm unsure why canonical or next or prev or tag are in the HTML spec instead of in the extensions list.
